content.comment_body: Hello all, I would appreciate assistance connecting a 4-20mA signal generator to an [product_name] analog module. Should I connect the "o" of the generator to "I1" on the [product_name] module, and the "4-20mA" to the "+24V" terminal? Thanks in advance. (See attached image for reference.)

No. If the sensor has its own power supply, and that supply matches the [product_name] analog module power source, then: Connect the 0V (signal -) to Mx (such as M1 in your situation) and connect signal + to Ix (such as I1). If the supplies differ, join the M (0V) terminals of both power sources. Then, connect the 0V (signal -) to Mx (like M1), and signal + to Ix (like I1).

Thank you very much [user_name]. So, it's actually the reverse of what I suggested? I'm a bit confused because typically the (-) of the power supply is connected to the M1 terminal of the analog module, with the (+24VDC) connected to the (+) of the analog sensor, and the (-) of the analog sensor going to I1 on the module. I hope I'm interpreting this correctly.

Hello [user_name], What you're outlining applies when the sensor does not have an independent power source. In this situation, the sensor is a configurable current/voltage transmitter featuring its own power supply.
